keyFindings.description: pg_disk_watch has no liveness rule: after a SIGKILL of the step command it loops for ever (a kubectl exec df every 30 s, an error line each time), and since step and job names repeat across runs, a later run's low disk makes the orphan record pg_disk in the dead step's directory and runner_stop the new run's job of the same name.

readStepCopy returns ok for a copy with no phase, so a run recorded before phase existed never falls back to the name rules: a quick run's 300 s 10x-hour lands in the knee series; the comment at curves.go:149-150 and the README say such runs fall back.

A heap.txt-only copy failure (runner_copy_back returns 1 after every other file landed) now fails the step with the detail 'the step's files are missing here', which is false, and drops a valid row from the curves; heap.txt only feeds codepaths' MemStats, which copes without it.
The failed-kinds note leaves out loadgen_exit; curves.go's note lists it.
The PID-namespace comparison is written three times (pid_ns_check, down_run, cmd_status).
Dead fallbacks: ${ALL_KEEP_FOR:-$KEEP_FOR_DEFAULT} after ALL_KEEP_FOR is always set, and cmd_hold's '|| die' after use_run proved the directory.
The seed-counts case greps the SQL text out of kubectl.log and repeats the key list; assert the behaviour (seed.meta.json's counts keys) or the one constant instead.
